key_insight: A 3D COMSOL opto-electro-thermal model shows that an n-ZnSe/p-SrScCu3Se4/p+-WSe2 heterostructure can reach high photovoltaic performance when absorber width, doping, and defect levels are optimized.
engineering_relevance: The study suggests SrScCu3Se4 is a strong candidate absorber for high-efficiency, thermally aware chalcogenide solar-cell design in realistic device architectures.
method: Self-consistent coupling of optical generation, drift-diffusion transport, and thermal loss
Parameter sweep of absorber width, acceptor density, and bulk defects
evidence_signal: Under optimized conditions, the device achieved VOC 1.02 V, JSC 32.472 mA/cm2, FF 88.212%, and PCE 29.217%, with QE strong in the visible but reduced in the near-infrared.
watch_item: Results are simulation-based, so experimental validation is still needed to confirm material quality, interface behavior, and thermal stability in fabricated devices.
paper_title: Computational analysis and performance optimization of SrScCu3Se4-based solar cells using COMSOL Multiphysics
